name: Magento (Adobe Commerce)
verdict: No central app: each merchant admin creates and activates an OAuth 1.0a integration under System → Integrations and your app receives per-store credentials. No review, 1-3 days, though host firewalls can block paths.
needGuide: Yes — OAuth 1.0a signing and the merchant activation callback are fiddly, so follow the integration guide.

auth.detail: Per-store integration: merchant creates an Integration in Admin, which generates a consumer key/secret. On activation the store POSTs the key, secret, verifier and base URL to your callback URL, opens your identity link URL for merchant login, then you call /oauth/token/request and /oauth/token/access with HMAC-SHA256 signed requests. The access token is long-lived until revoked. Applies to PaaS (on-prem/cloud); Adobe Commerce cloud-service customers use a different auth method.

effort.timeToProduction: 1-3 days (no review) for the integration; Marketplace listing timing unknown

approval.gate: None for the OAuth 1.0a handshake: each merchant admin activates it. Distributing an extension as code is optional through Adobe Commerce Marketplace (listing review not retrieved).

scopes.why: The merchant ticks API resources in an ACL tree when creating the integration; no scope names or review triggers.
scopes.summary: The merchant picks which API resources (ACL tree) the integration may access during creation; there are no scope names or review triggers. Access is all-or-nothing per resource list.

cost: Free for Magento Open Source; Adobe Commerce requires a merchant license. Developer needs no fee for the integration.
prerequisites: Account and owner: Any developer. Needs a public HTTPS callback and identity-link page that can authenticate your own user and map them to the store.
Where you register: No central registration. Merchant Admin → System → Extensions → Integrations → Add New Integration → set callback and identity link URLs and API resources → Save & Activate.
Cost: Free for Magento Open Source; Adobe Commerce requires a merchant license. Developer needs no fee for the integration.

registerAt.path: No central registration. Merchant Admin → System → Extensions → Integrations → Add New Integration → set callback and identity link URLs and API resources → Save & Activate.

steps.do: Stand up a test Magento store and enable HTTPS
Build the callback endpoint to receive the activation POST (store URL, verifier, consumer key/secret) and store them
Build the identity link page: merchant logs into your app, then you call POST /oauth/token/request and /oauth/token/access with signed parameters
Merchant creates the integration (callback URL, identity link URL, resource ACL) and clicks Save and Activate
Call REST (for example GET /rest/V1/products) with the signed Authorization header and validate success
Handle revocation (merchant deletes or deactivates the integration) and re-activation
Optional: package an extension for Adobe Commerce Marketplace

roles.team: Any developer. Needs a public HTTPS callback and identity-link page that can authenticate your own user and map them to the store.
roles.console: none documented (no developer console for Integrations; Adobe Developer Console applies to other Adobe APIs).
roles.customer: A store admin with access to System → Integrations and to the API resources being granted creates and activates the integration, and clicks Allow. Hosting WAF/CDN rules can block /rest or /oauth paths.

testing: Use a local Magento Open Source or Adobe Commerce cloud dev environment and Adobe's sample PHP scripts (endpoint.php, login.php, checklogin.php) that simulate the flow.
Installing via Composer likely needs Commerce Marketplace access keys.

blockers.problem: OAuth 1.0a signing is easy to get wrong
blockers.fix: Reuse an existing library (such as PHPoAuthLib in the Adobe samples).

blockers.problem: The merchant must correctly paste both callback and identity link URLs
Cloud-service/SaaS Commerce customers use a different auth path
CDN or firewall rules often block /oauth and /rest calls from your server IPs

automation.agentCan: Write the signing client, callback and identity-link endpoints, the customer setup guide with exact field values, and revocation handling.
automation.humanMust: The customer's admin must log in, create and activate the integration; a human accepts any Marketplace agreement.

uncertain: Adobe Commerce Marketplace review, the standalone-bearer-token option for integration tokens, and the Adobe IMS / App Builder route for cloud-service customers were not retrieved.
Per-integration ACL details beyond the OAuth page were not checked.
